CSCI2720 Building Web Applications

HTTP

HTTP (HyperText Transfer Protocol) is an stateless Application Layer protocol for transferring data.

Example: GET / HTTP/1.1, HTTP/1.1 200 OK

Headers: User-Agent, Referer, Cookie, Content-Type, Accept-*, [reply] Cache-Control, Set-Cookie, Content-Disposition

URL (Uniform Resource Locator): Protocol + Hostname + Path + Filename + Query + Hash

Socket: Transport Protocol + IP Address + Port Number, endpoint of transfer.

HTML

HTML (HyperText Markup Language) is invented by Sir Tim Berners-Lee at CERN to share scientific knowledge, maintained by W3C and WHATWG.

Common tags: <!DOCTYPE>, <head> (useful data, not shown; e.g. favicon, page title, metadata), <body> (all shown stuff),<h1> (heading), <p> (paragraph), <!-- --> (comment), <a> (link; href, target: _self, _blank).

Semantic elements: Organised into logical sections, for easier bot scraping and anchor point for styling CSS.

Image: <img src, width, height> <svg width, height><circle cx, cy, r, fill></circle></svg>

HTML Encoding: &lt; &gt; &nbsp;

HTTP Requests: GET (encode in URL: limited data size + can be bookmarked + stay in browser history / server log) / POST (data in request body: data size only limited by body size)

CSS and Bootstrap

CSS (Cascading Style Sheets) is for separation of content and presentation.

Override Order: External Style Sheet (.css; link, rel="stylesheet", href) < Interal Style Sheet (head) < Inline Styles (style attr) < !important

Selectors: #id, .class, tag, [attr="value"], :hover, :nth_child(3), ::first_letter

Length Units: px (pixel), em (rel. current font size), rem (rel. root font size), % (size of same prop. of parent), vh / vw (1% of viewport height / width)

Block-Level: full width, force new line; Inline: occupy content width, start anywhere

Hide Element: display: none (not occupy space); visibility: hidden (occupy space);

Positioning: position: absolute | fixed | relative

Bootstrap: (Button) .btn, .btn-primary; (Icon) .bi, bi-airplane; (Grid) breakpoints: sm (>= 576px), md (>= 768px), lg (>= 992px), xl(>= 1200px), xxl(>= 1400px), .container-*, .row, .col-*-x (/12)

Javascript

Basics

Javascript: Interpreted, Single-threaded, Multi-paradigm (Object-Oriented / Imperative / Functional)

Data Types: String, Number, Boolean

String Functions: String.trim, String.split, Interpolation `\${variable}`, '/^[^\s@]+@[^\s@]+\.[^\s@]+\$/'.test (email)

Function: function(){}, () => { return a; }, () => a;

Fetch API: fetch(file, {method: 'GET/POST/PUT', body: '1234'}).then(res => res.text()).then(data => ...).catch(err => console.error(err))

Asynchrony

Call Stack: Single Thread + Blocking. Event Loop brings event from Callback Queue to Call Stack when is empty

Scheduling (X = Timeout / Interval): setX(() => {}, 2000); clearX();

Callback Hell: Nested callback functions. Resolved by Promise[pending, fulfilled, rejected].

Promise: Run by new Promise((onResolve, onReject) => {}); Collect result by promise.then((val) => {}, (err) => {})

Async/await: Promise can be awaited for result in async functions (only).

DOM (Document Object Model)

Manipulate DOM Element: document.querySelector[All] (return NodeList, i.e., all nodes, including text node), document.getElementById, document.getElementsBy[Class/Tag]Name (return HTMLCollection, i.e., element node only), document.[images/links/scripts], .setAttribute, .appendChild

Event Listener: addEventListener(type = 'hover', listener = (event) => {})

Scope: Arrow function no scope, so this refers to the parent one.

Functions

Declaration: function func(para1, para2="Hello", ...rest) { console.log(arguments) }. JS Function be nested.

IIFE (Immediately-Invoked Function Expression): (func() {})()

Generator Function: function*, yield, next()

Arrays

Array, kind of object, which are passed by reference. [...a, b] = [1, 2, 3]

Functions: length, slice(start, [end]) (unmodified), splice(start, [deleteCount, [itemToAdd]]); pop/push: end of array, shift/unshift: begin of array; indexOf, lastIndexOf, includes; find, filter; reverse, split, join, map, forEach. Function parameters: (val, idx, arr) => {}. Support negative index.

Loop Object Key/Value: for (const x in/of A).

NodeList vs HTMLCollection: Both array-like, can convert via Array.from(). NodeList is static and does not support filter, whereas HTMLCollection is live and does not support forEach / find.

React JS

Functional Component: function Welcome(props) { return (<h1>Hello {props.name}</h1>) }; function App() { return (<div><Welcome name="you"/></div>) }

Class Component: class App extends React.Component { constructor() { super(); this.state = {value: 0}; }; buttonClicked = () => this.setState(...); render() { return (<>{this.props.good ? this.props.name : ""}</>); } }

Render: const root = ReactDOM.createRoot(document.querySelector('#app')); root.render(<App />). Have Virtual DOM, and only update when changed.

Event Listener: camelCase.

Node JS

Routing: app.get('/login/:user', (req, res) => { res.send(req.params); // :user; req.query returns after ?, both as assoc array }); app.get('/download', (req, res) => { res.sendFile("index.html")})

Single Page Application (SPA)

Pros: efficient use of bandwidth, separation of view and data and easier to maintain, improve UX without obvious reloading

Cons: browser history not trivial for bookmarking, SEO not work since content not scraped easily, dependent on JS and thin server, thick client

Cookies and Sessions

Cookies: Embedded in HTTP header, stored in client browser, auto send back to server in subsequent requests. (Set-Cookie: name1=value1;name2=value2, Cookie: name1=value1;name2=value2); Expires, Max-Age, Domain, Path. Express: res.cookie(name, value[, options])

Session: Store sessions on server and generates a session ID for each unique visitor.

Storage: localStorage / sessionStorage. setItem, getItem, removeItem, clear.
